question: What was the theme of Financial Literacy Week 2025 observed from 24 to 28 February?

options.text: Credit Discipline and Credit from Formal Institutions
Financial Literacy: A Step Towards Empowerment

solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Financial Literacy Week 2025 focused on the theme **"Financial Literacy - Women's Prosperity"**, aiming to empower women through financial knowledge.
 
• The initiative was spearheaded by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to promote financial education and inclusion among women.
 
• Various workshops, campaigns, and educational programs were conducted to highlight the importance of savings, investments, and formal credit access for women.
 
• The theme emphasized the need for gender equality in financial literacy to ensure women's active participation in economic activities.
 
• It underscored the significance of financial independence for women, contributing to their socio-economic empowerment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Literacy**

 
 
• Financial literacy refers to the ability to understand and effectively use financial skills such as budgeting, investing, and personal financial management.
 
• It plays a crucial role in improving financial decision-making and promoting economic stability.
 
• Enhanced financial literacy can help individuals avoid financial pitfalls and achieve long-term financial goals.
 
 
 
• **Role of RBI in Financial Literacy**
 
 
• The RBI organizes Financial Literacy Week annually to promote awareness about various financial topics.
 
• It collaborates with banks and educational institutions to implement programs targeting different segments of the population.
 
 
 
• **Gender Equality in Financial Inclusion**
 
 
• Empowering women through financial literacy contributes to reducing the gender gap in financial access and decision-making.
 
• It enhances women's participation in formal economic sectors and fosters sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **Previous Themes of Financial Literacy Week**
 
 
• 2023: "Good Financial Behaviour – Your Saviour"
 
• 2024: "Credit Discipline and Credit from Formal Institutions"
